skill.name: session-handoff
skill.description: Write a HANDOFF.md that lets a fresh agent session continue the work, with goal, state, decisions, next steps and traps. Use when ending a long session, hitting context limits or switching agents.
skill.summary: Create a concise handoff with verified repository state, decisions, ordered next steps, and unresolved questions.
skill.author: agentkitco

security_audit.summary: All five static findings are false positives: Markdown backticks, read-only Git inspection, and verification placeholders explain the matches. No evidence found of prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent in SKILL.md. The workflow writes a handoff document and may run project tests, so repository trust and normal tool permissions still matter.

content.value_statement: Long sessions and agent switches can lose decisions, test results, and unfinished work. This skill creates a concise HANDOFF.md with verified state and actionable next steps.
actual_capabilities: Inspect Git status, the current branch, and the ten most recent commits.
Write HANDOFF.md in the repository root or a user-selected location, targeting fewer than about 80 lines.
Record goals, completed work, unfinished changes, decisions, and rejected alternatives.
Document available test or build results, including exact failing commands and error text.
List ordered next steps, known traps, open questions, and unverified claims.
Explain how to resume from the handoff without committing it unless requested.
limitations: Requires access to the current session context and repository to verify project state.
Test and build verification depends on available tools, dependencies, and execution permissions.
Does not automatically transfer conversation history or start another agent session.
Cannot guarantee that recorded facts remain accurate after later repository changes.

use_cases.title: Pause unfinished development
use_cases.description: Capture unfinished changes, test results, and next steps before ending a coding session.

use_cases.title: Transfer an investigation
use_cases.description: Record reproduction commands, exact errors, rejected approaches, and unresolved questions for the next investigator.

use_cases.title: Coordinate agent changes
use_cases.description: Provide another agent with verified project state and ordered actions without requiring the full conversation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Create HANDOFF.md for this session. Include the goal, current state, and next steps. Do not commit it.

prompt_templates.title: Verify project state
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a handoff after checking Git status, branch, and recent commits. Run quick tests if available and permitted. Mark anything unverified.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: preserve verified repository and test status.

prompt_templates.title: Transfer a blocked investigation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a debugging handoff with exact failing commands, errors, rejected approaches, and questions requiring my decision. Exclude secrets and personal data.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare another agent to resume
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a handoff under about 80 lines for another agent. Separate verified facts from assumptions, identify unfinished files, and order actionable next steps. Do not commit.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: switch agents near a context limit.

output_examples.input: Prepare a handoff for an unfinished search filter change.
output: Goal: finish the search filter update.
Current state: the filter change is incomplete; tests have not been run.
Decision: preserve the existing query format to avoid changing callers.
Next steps: finish input validation, run focused tests, and review the final diff.
Not verified: behavior with empty search input.

output_examples.input: Hand off a failing build when the full error output is unavailable.
output: Current state: a build failure was reported, but its exact command and error are unavailable.
Open question: which build command produced the failure?
Next steps: reproduce the failure, record the exact command and error, and investigate the first failing step.
Not verified: the reported failure and its cause.

best_practices: Verify repository state immediately before writing, and distinguish completed checks from assumptions.
Keep next steps specific and ordered; include exact commands and errors for observed failures.
Review the handoff for secrets, tokens, and personal data, and keep it uncommitted unless explicitly requested.
anti_patterns: Treating remembered test results as current verification without rerunning or labeling them.
Writing vague next steps that require access to the previous conversation.
Including credentials or accidentally committing session notes to a shared branch.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates HANDOFF.md with goals, verified state, decisions, ordered next steps, known traps, open questions, and unverified claims.

faq.question: Which tools are listed as supported?
faq.answer: The listing supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Repository inspection and file writing require appropriate tool access.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: It asks the agent to run quick project tests or a build when possible. Checks that were not run must remain labeled unverified.

faq.question: Will it commit the handoff?
faq.answer: No. The instructions prohibit committing the handoff unless asked and require warning about accidental inclusion on a shared branch.

faq.question: Can I choose a different output location?
faq.answer: Yes. The default is the repository root, but you can specify another path.

faq.question: How do I resume work later?
faq.answer: Start a new session and ask the agent to read HANDOFF.md and continue. The file does not automatically restore the previous conversation.
